_doc: ULTRASTABILITY-1 (Rowan, 2026-11-17): the platform's name is a design rule from W. Ross Ashby (Design for a Brain, 1952). A system is ultrastable when two loops keep its essential variables inside bounds: a fast first-order loop that corrects ordinary disturbance without changing the system, and a slow second-order loop that, when a variable stays out of bounds, makes a discrete step change to the system's own parameters or structure and keeps the change only if the variable returns; after the ladder it keeps searching untried parameter values until one holds the variable (ASHBY-SEARCH-1). Every variable has limits (ASHBY-1). Read by foundation/ultrastability.py; checked by `python3 -m foundation ultrastability --check`; rendered on /how from site/ultrastability-data.js (generated). Never edit a bound to clear a breach: bounds are the viability limits, changed only by a PR with a lineage note.
credit: W. Ross Ashby, Design for a Brain (1952)

variables.name: Spend against budget
variables.why: Past 1.0 the system costs more than its owner accepts, so it is no longer viable.

ladder.what: wake the executor less often
restructure: find and cut the spend source

variables.name: Verified deploys
variables.why: A deploy whose live code differs from its commit means the loop that ships is not closing.

ladder.what: shift executor capacity to deploy repairs (raise the repair-deploys weight)
restructure: repair the deploy path that failed verification

variables.name: Words that no longer match code
variables.why: A public statement the code no longer makes true breaks the system's own record of itself.

ladder.what: shift executor capacity to say-do fixes (raise the repair-claims weight)
restructure: bind or regenerate the drifting statements

variables.name: Verified deploys per unit of cost and human touch (k)
variables.why: Below the floor the system ships less than it costs to run, so the work stops compounding.

ladder.what: wake the executor more often
restructure: remove what keeps deploys from shipping

variables.name: Clocks that stopped
variables.why: A clock that stops halts the loop it drives; the system is viable only while every clock keeps ticking, and a watchdog that goes silent reads as unmeasured.

ladder.what: declare a stall sooner so the restart comes earlier
restructure: add an independent trigger to the clock that keeps stopping

variables.name: Front-end findings that block a user
variables.why: A page that fails accessibility, leaks backend detail, breaks its structure or its brand is a front end drifting into a mishmash; the UI/UX loop (UIUX-1) must keep this at zero, and a variable that cannot be read from a fresh audit is unmeasured and so not in bounds.

ladder.what: shift executor capacity to front-end fixes (raise the repair-ui weight)
restructure: move the failing rule into the shared component or design token so each page inherits the fix

variables.name: User paths that still walk end to end
variables.why: A path in doctrine/stakeholders.json that no longer clicks through is a user who cannot get from entry to the next step; every audience path must walk, and the UI/UX loop runs each as a browser flow.

ladder.what: shift executor capacity to broken user paths (raise the repair-ui weight)
restructure: repair the broken step or change the path in doctrine/stakeholders.json so it matches the page

variables.name: Unattended horizon
variables.why: A year with no person is the design target (UNATTENDED-365). foundation/yearsim.py injects a year of faults into the real recovery code; when the 10th percentile of simulated years ends before 365 days, something the system needs is not repairing itself.

ladder.what: shift executor capacity to whatever ends the simulated year (raise the unattended-year weight)
restructure: build the recovery mechanism for the fault class that ends the simulated year first

variables.name: Self-originated releases
variables.unit: substantive server-originated changes a day (14-day mean, at least 10 changed code lines each)
variables.why: Rowan's biggest goal: the server itself originates and ships substantive changes daily (SELF-REFERENCE-1). Counted from git by foundation/yearsim.py self_commits: executor or own-agent commits on main with at least 10 changed lines of code outside ledgers and generated data. A one-line import removal is upkeep, not a release (NO-TRIVIAL-COMMITS).

ladder.what: wake the executor more often
shift executor capacity to its own repair (raise the self-shipping weight)
restructure: find why the executor's items fail and change its route (model rung, patch format, item size)

variables.name: Owner interventions
variables.why: Every time Rowan has to notice a problem and redirect the system in chat, he is acting as the second loop. Ultrastable means the system does that itself. Counted from provenance: distinct thread sessions that changed the repository.

ladder.what: absorb: turn each recent owner intervention into a variable, bound, detector or rule here, so the same message is not needed again
restructure: the intervention kinds that keep recurring get their own essential variable with a ladder

variables.name: Second-loop steps that worked
variables.unit: share of the last 30 verdicts kept
variables.why: A slow loop whose changes are all undone is moving, not learning; that was the state before SECOND-LOOP-2.

ladder.what: give a parameter step more ticks before judging it
act only on variables that stay out longer (fewer steps on noise)
restructure: find the ladders whose steps keep being undone and replace those steps

variables.name: Work items an agent cannot misread
variables.unit: share of open items with done check, prediction, out-of-scope line and live proof
variables.why: unlearn.dev lesson: a vague item gets a plausible wrong fix. An item passes foundation/specgate.py only with all four parts.

ladder.what: rewrite the open items that miss a part so they pass specgate, from their own source code
restructure: make the filer of each failing item write all four parts (fix the writer, not the item)

variables.name: Research findings true in code
variables.unit: share of findings in every paper whose own measurement meets its target
variables.why: RESEARCH-LOOP-1 (Rowan, 2026-11-25): 'make sure your code reflects your own R&D ... that's an open loop too'. Every finding names its mechanism paths and the metric that tests it; research --check fails a missing path, and this variable fails a finding the system does not live up to.

ladder.what: build: for each finding that is not met, change the mechanism it names until its metric meets the target (research files Q-RES items; take them first)
restructure: a finding still not met after its items closed gets a new mechanism, a new ladder here, or its paper states the gap with the number

variables.name: Lessons enforced in code
variables.unit: share of lessons in doctrine/lessons.json bound to a check, variable, detector or test
variables.why: LESSONS-1 (Rowan, 2026-11-25): a lesson that lives in chat is learned again the hard way. Each one is bound to code, or carried by an open item until it is.

ladder.what: build: take the Q-LESSON items and bind each lesson to a check, variable, detector or test

tenant.what: Every system built on Ultrastable declares the same four variables at bootstrap; the platform loop runs them for tenant 0 only

variables.name: Uptime
variables.why: The system has to be reachable to be improved.

ladder.what: run fewer live apps, so each one gets more of the free-tier capacity
iterate: change the app
retire: stop spending on what cannot stay up

variables.name: Spend against the declared monthly budget
variables.why: The owner accepted a running cost; past it the system is not viable.

ladder.what: lower the per-app daily request cap (a soft throttle)
iterate: cut the spend source
retire: stop spending

variables.name: Words that no longer match code
variables.why: A tenant's public statements stay true.

ladder.what: launch fewer new apps a day, leaving capacity for upkeep
iterate: regenerate the statements from code

variables.name: The tenant's own declared value metric
variables.why: A system with no measure that can be wrong cannot be improved. Read as the tenant's declared metric divided by its own declared target (ops/tenants/<slug>.json declared_metric, declared_target); 1.0 is on target.

ladder.what: launch only higher-scoring ideas
iterate: change what the app does
retire: the measured value does not justify the cost

self.name: ultrastable
self.is: A system that keeps its own essential variables inside bounds with two loops: a fast loop that corrects ordinary disturbance without changing the system, and a slow loop that changes the system's own parameters or structure when a variable stays out of bounds, and keeps the change only if the variable returns.
does: reads every essential variable against its bounds on a clock, from ledgers its own loops write
corrects disturbance with its regulators (the fast loop) without changing itself
when a variable stays out of bounds, takes one discrete step on that variable's ladder (the slow loop), then keeps or undoes it by the next readings
records every reading, step and verdict with provenance, and treats an unreadable variable as unmeasured, never as fine
declares what it is and what it consists of in this model, and fails its own build when running code and this model differ
self.not: It does not wait on a person to close a loop. The only pauses are the irreversible, identity-bound acts listed under the boundary.

inheritance.rule: Improve once, improve all: a change to the foundation or the seed reaches every system built on Ultrastable, because tenants are bootstrapped from the same kit and declare the same essential variables.

_doc_settle: SECOND-LOOP-SETTLE-1 (2026-11-21): a param step is judged after settle_ticks readings, because a parameter acts at once. An item or spinoff step is work the executor must do first, so judging it after 3 readings reverted all 14 of them before any could act (0 of 14 kept, ops/ultrastability.jsonl to 2026-11-21). It is kept as soon as the variable is back in bounds, reverted when its item reaches a final status with the variable still out, or after item_settle_ticks readings.
_doc_second_loop_2: SECOND-LOOP-2 (Rowan, 2026-11-25): 'I'm still not getting the ultra stable part.' Three variables added that measure the second loop itself: how often a person had to act as the second loop (owner_interventions, target 0), whether its own steps work (second_loop_keep_rate; until now every verdict was a revert) and whether work items can be misread (spec_quality, SPEC-GATE-1). A tenant value shared by every tenant is a sensor fault (common_mode) and is held. readiness() is the one-year score published on /ultrastability.
